summary: Kavita Singh (1964–2023) worked in art history and Indology. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College, MS University of Baroda, and Panjab University. A founder of Jawaharlal Nehru University, she served there as dean, alongside roles at Marg Publications and other institutions.

Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and Tshampa Norbu, later serving as its headmaster (c. 1906–1919) and lecturing at the University of Calcutta in 1920.

Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) was an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Kyushu University by 1992. His career included serving as a lecturer at the University of Miyazaki and as professor emeritus at Seijo University (c. 1968–1995).

Kazuaki Komine (born 1947) specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned undergraduate and doctoral degrees from Waseda University and held posts at Waseda Jitsugyo High School, Tokushima University, the National Institute of Japanese Literature, and Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

Kazuaki Tanahashi (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center from 1977 to 1984 and became a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki (born 1946) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He served on the faculty at Shuchiin University, where he was attested as assistant professor (1982–1988) and professor emeritus (2006–2013).

Kazuharu Mizuno (born 1958) works in Tibetology and geography. He earned degrees from Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University, and served as a geography professor at Kyoto University from approximately 2009 to 2024.

Kazuhiko Atsumi (1928–2019) worked in philosophy and related fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo from 1948 to 1954, later holding academic posts there (c. 1964–1989) and at Suzuka University of Medical Science (c. 1991–2003).

Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) works in linguistics, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Sophia, Kyoto, Cornell (under Jay Jasanoff), and Osaka universities, he held professorships at Nagoya City Women's College, Kyoto University (c. 1999–2020), and Nagoya City University.

Kazuhiro Kawasaki (born 1974) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at Koyasan University. He has held positions there as a researcher (attested 2005) and special appointed professor (attested 2026).

Kazuhiro Yamamoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Silpakorn University, completing doctoral work under the supervision of Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya (attested 2009).
Kazuma Teshima specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He has served as a professor at Rissho University, with his faculty appointments attested in 2015 and 2026.

Kazunobu Matsuda (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and under Shiro Matsumoto, later holding faculty posts at Otani University (attested 1985–1989) and Bukkyo University (attested 1995–2024).

Kazuo Hyodo (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and completed his PhD at Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, later serving as an assistant professor at Otani University from around 1984 to 2014.

Kazuo Kano (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned an MA at Kyoto University under Katsumi Mimaki and a PhD at Hamburg under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, later teaching at Koyasan University and Komazawa University.

Kazuo Okabe (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, subsequently teaching at Aichi Gakuin University and serving as a professor at Komazawa University from 1979 to 2006.

Kazuo Osumi (born 1933) is a scholar of Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. He completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo, later serving as an assistant professor at Hokkaido University and professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).
Kazuo Oyamada (born 1952) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Tamagawa University and held an academic post at Rissho University.

Kazutoshi Ueda (1867–1937) was a linguist and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Georg von der Gabelentz. He founded the Linguistic Society of Japan and held posts at the University of Tokyo, Kokugakuin University, and Kogakkan University.

Kazuyoshi Hotta works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo, where he also served as director of the Buddhist Youth Association (attested 2007), and was an assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).
